subject: Key gateway audit: operator split + offline rotation workflow
messages:
From: Craig Humphrey <craig.humphrey@finsys.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: secops-team@finsys.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: FinCo audit: key gateway & operator separation questions

Jordan / Soojin —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our internal security review flagged a few items we need clarified before we sign the connectivity agreement for the private deployment:

1) We need a clear operator separation model for the HSM/KMS bridge — who has physical vs logical control, and what controls prevent a single operator from reconstructing keys.
2) Offline rotation process — we require an air-gapped plan for emergency rotation and proof that key material can be rotated without exposing plaintext to the cloud/host.
3) Network egress and bastion constraints — we have strict firewall rules; the bridge must support a highly restricted outbound path and attestations for any update.

Can you share any existing runbooks or a short one-page workflow for the rotation + operator split? Also need any artifacts for our auditors (attestation checklist, network diff).

Appreciate a quick reply — our procurement cadence is timeboxed.

Thanks,
Craig
Senior InfoSec Manager — FinCo Systems

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Craig Humphrey <craig.humphrey@finsys.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FinCo audit: key gateway & operator separation questions

Craig —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching a short packet (key-gateway-proposal-v1.pdf) and an operator separation checklist. High level answers below; we can walk the audit team through the plan.

1) Operator separation: Redwood supports a split-operator model. We separate the roles: "Custody Operators" (customer-controlled KMS/HSM admins) vs "Platform Operators" (Redwood runtime operators). Our recommended deployment for FinCo is: customer-controlled HSM in your VPC or on-prem; Redwood runs a stateless gateway proxy in a restricted subnet. The gateway receives wrapped keys only; unwrap/usage happens inside the customer HSM. Platform Operators never touch unwrapped key material.

2) Offline rotation: We include an emergency offline rotation workflow that leverages split key shares and an offline signing ceremony. The procedure uses threshold-wrapping to produce new KEKs, and the cloud bridge only transmits signed artifacts — no plaintext moves off-prem. The runbook includes human approvals, time-stamped attestations, and an audit trail (see operator-separation-checklist.xlsx).

3) Network egress: The gateway uses a single egress flow through a customer-managed bastion with mTLS and allowlisted destinations. We can provide a network diff for the minimal firewall changes we need; no outbound SSH required from the HSM cluster.

Next steps: propose an architecture review call with your auditors Wednesday 11/11 at 10:00 PT. If that works, we'll send a read-ahead.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Director of Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Craig Humphrey <craig.humphrey@finsys.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FinCo audit: key gateway & operator separation questions

Craig / team —

Quick technical clarifications ahead of the call:

- The design attaches a "wrapped-key-only" policy to the gateway so even if the gateway is compromised, the attacker cannot derive plaintext. The HSM enforces KMS policies and requires a local unwrapping operation.
- For the offline rotation procedure we rely on an HSM-supported key ceremony (FIPS/HSM vendor feature). Our runbook outlines when to use threshold unwrapping vs full-key import.
- We also added SHA-256 signed attestations from the HSM for each wrap/unwrap action; those sigs are shipped to your auditor endpoint for verification.

I've attached network-isolation-diff.txt that highlights the firewall ports/hosts we request. We'll keep outbound to a single management endpoint and accept your allowlist.

Sooj —
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Private Deploys

This is helpful. Two audit follow-ups: 1) we need a short proof of concept showing the offline rotation without connecting to Redwood control plane (airgapped flow), and 2) examples of the attestation artifacts in a format our SIEM can consume. Can you commit to a PoC window before EOW (Fri)?

If so, please include a minimal list of personnel we should expect during the ceremony (we'll only allow named operators access).

Craig

Craig —

We can run the PoC on Thursday 11/12 in your environment or in a mutually controlled lab. Proposed scope:

- Offline rotation rehearsal using a detached HSM appliance (vendor-supplied USB-token/HSM module emulation) and threshold share recomposition.
- Produce audit artifacts: signed wrap/unwrap logs, signed key IDs, and a zipped attestation bundle in JSON (SIEM-friendly).
- Operator list: Mina Haddad (Redwood Custody Lead, approval signer), Ben Carter (Platform Run Ops, observer only), Frank Lyons (Customer Custody Operator — named by FinCo), and 2 FinCo auditable witnesses.

We'll limit Redwood personnel with signing capability — only the Custody Lead will carry signing authority for the ceremony; Platform Run Ops will have observer-only permissions per our separation model. We'll deliver sample attestation artifacts in advance for your SIEM ingest test.

Confirm the time and whether you want this in your lab or our controlled lab; we can provide the minimal cabling and a one-page preflight checklist.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Head of Custody Integrations — Redwood Inference
